news.title: Divine Leads Media Deploys DLM ResultDesk Across First Wave of Pilot Schools
news.author: Joshua Eesuola
news.summary: Our field engineering team completed the deployment of DLM ResultDesk across partner secondary schools, ending manual broadsheet errors for over 1,200 students.
news.content:
Our field deployment team has successfully completed the installation and configuration of DLM ResultDesk across our initial partner secondary schools in Lagos.

Teachers were trained on entering continuous assessments (CA) and examination marks directly into the system. Within minutes, the software computed weighted averages, class positions, and generated standard student report sheets.

Initial feedback highlights that result compilation time was reduced from 2 weeks of manual calculations to under 2 hours.

news.title: Low-Power Computer Lab Hardware Bench-Testing Completed
news.author: DLM Hardware Lab
news.summary: We bench-tested 40 low-power desktop PCs running on a single 1.5kVA solar inverter system to guarantee zero disruptions during school CBT exams.
news.content:
Power reliability remains the number one bottleneck for Nigerian school computer labs. In preparation for upcoming term examinations, our lab technicians stress-tested 40 ultra-low-power desktop setups.

Operating at an average load of only 18W per station, the entire 40-seater lab operated continuously for 6 hours on a modest solar inverter backup bank without a single system reboot.

This architecture ensures Nigerian schools can host JAMB and internal CBT mock exams without spending millions on daily generator diesel costs.

news.title: Practical Digital Economy & AI Workshop for Secondary Students
news.author: Joshua Eesuola
news.summary: Over 180 secondary school students completed our hands-on digital skills seminar, learning practical computing and how to use educational AI tools safely.
news.content:
We hosted our quarterly 'Practical Digital Skills for Future Leaders' workshop. Students moved beyond rote textbook computer studies to practical keyboard mastery, structured document creation, and introductory AI logic.

Participants learned how to prompt AI assistants for step-by-step problem breakdown in mathematics and sciences while learning the critical difference between factual verification and hallucination.

articles.title: Why Nigerian Schools Must Shift from Manual Broadsheets to Offline Software
articles.author: Eesuola Joshua Damilare
articles.summary: Manual broadsheet calculation costs Nigerian teachers hundreds of hours each term and leads to arithmetic errors. Here is why offline school software is the proven solution.
articles.content:
# Why Nigerian Schools Must Shift from Manual Broadsheets to Offline Software

At the end of every school term in Nigeria, teachers face the dreaded 'exam processing week'. Teachers spend countless late nights manually calculating continuous assessment (CA) scores, exam totals, weighted averages, and class rankings with pocket calculators.

## The Real Bottlenecks of Manual Calculation

1. **Arithmetic Human Error**: Calculating positions across 40 to 60 students in 12 different subjects manually results in frequent mathematical discrepancies.
2. **Teacher Burnout**: Valuable teaching and student mentoring time is consumed by repetitive arithmetic.
3. **Damaged Paper Records**: Water damage, lost broadsheets, and torn files make historical student record retrieval nearly impossible.

## Why Offline Software is Essential for Nigeria

Cloud-only school portals often fail in Nigeria because of unstable internet connectivity and expensive monthly subscriptions. **DLM ResultDesk** runs 100% offline, allowing teachers to record scores without waiting for network bars, instantly producing error-free broadsheets and report cards.

articles.title: Sizing Solar Inverter Systems for School Computer Labs in Nigeria
articles.author: DLM Hardware Lab
articles.summary: Running generators for school computer labs is financially unsustainable. Learn how to calculate exact power wattage and size battery backups for uninterrupted lab sessions.
articles.content:
# Sizing Solar Inverter Systems for School Computer Labs in Nigeria

With rising fuel costs across Nigeria, running a 5kVA or 10kVA petrol generator just to power a 30-computer lab for a 45-minute lesson is no longer sustainable.

## The Math of Low-Power Labs

Traditional bulky desktop towers consume between 120W and 200W each. Equipping a lab with 30 traditional desktops requires over 4,500 Watts of power.

By contrast, **DLM Certified Low-Power Desktops** consume only 15W to 25W each:

- 30 Low-Power Systems = ~600 Watts total load.
- A standard 1.5kVA or 2.5kVA Pure Sine Wave Inverter with two 200Ah deep-cycle tubular batteries can easily power the entire computer lab for 4 to 6 full hours.

Schools save over ₦250,000 monthly in diesel costs while eliminating examination interruptions.

articles.title: How to Safely Introduce AI Learning Tools to Secondary School Learners
articles.author: Eesuola Joshua Damilare
articles.coverAlt: Students learning in modern computer lab
articles.summary: Artificial Intelligence is already here. Here is how we teach secondary school learners to use AI to understand difficult subjects and build real skills.
articles.content:
# How to Safely Introduce AI Learning Tools to Secondary School Learners

Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the future of work. In Nigeria, our students should not just be passive consumers of technology; they must learn to utilize digital and AI tools to master school subjects and build problem-solving capabilities.

## Core Principles for Classroom AI Training

1. **AI as a Socratic Tutor, Not an Answer Bot**: Teach students to ask AI to explain concepts with local Nigerian analogies rather than copying essay answers.
2. **Verification & Fact Checking**: Show students examples of AI hallucination so they develop critical thinking.
3. **Practical Keyboard & Digital Fluency**: Theoretical knowledge must be grounded with fast typing, document formatting, and local computing fluency.
